title: Sixteen Sales and One Marked Tag
subtitle: 消费与折扣 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 消费与折扣（社会服务与人际沟通·经济消费与折扣）
meta: 主题语境：消费与折扣（社会服务与人际沟通·经济消费与折扣）　|　核心词汇：discount　|　正文 343 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 discount 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1956 the shopkeeper ① gave a discount that no trader in the market would have matched, and he said the giving was the whole of the sale. The ② discount, meaning the reduction and not the deduction, ran sixteen sales and stayed unmarked on the tag; a discount, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left unpriced.

Every ③ discount in that shop had the same marked tag at the corner of it, and the ④ discount at the end, meaning the one they kept for the winter coats and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever asked for twice. A discount, his assistant said, is nine parts counting and one part somebody willing to give; the shopkeeper said the counting is the part that fills sixteen sales.

The accountant meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the discount was the whole of the invoice, meaning the deduction and not the reduction. The ⑥ discount, meaning the deduction and not any of that, is the only thing on an invoice that everybody enters and nobody explains; discount, she said, is either something you give or the only word that means both a reduction and a deduction. She said the deduction is the part they remember.

By 1964 the ⑦ discount had become a line in a notice, and the notice had become an argument about the marked tag. The ⑧ discount of the whole thing, the shopkeeper wrote in November, was one shop and sixteen sales of counting; discount, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to count. She said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ discount I remember is the one at the end, which was given in 1979 and is still described as the strangest in the shop. A ⑩ discount, the assistant said in 1981, is the only thing that improves by being explained; every discount, she said, is a deduction that has agreed to look like a reduction. She said the deduction was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 折扣；减价（指店里给出的那一个）
B. n. 折扣（指那个减价本身，与那笔扣款相对）
C. 固定搭配：give a discount 给出一个折扣
D. n. 折扣（指留给冬季外套用的那一个）
E. n. 折扣；打折（抽象总称，指一家店铺的全部让利）
F. n. 折扣（指通告上写到、被公示的那一个）
G. n. 折扣额；扣款（指发票上被记入的那笔）
H. n. 扣款（抽象总称，指人人入账却无人解释的那笔）

items.q: gave a discount that no trader in the market would have matched
The discount, meaning the reduction and not the deduction
the discount was the whole of the invoice
the discount had become a line in a notice
The discount of the whole thing
A discount, the assistant said in 1981

answers.why: give a discount 意为“给出一个折扣”，1956 年店主给了一个市场上没有一位商人比得上的折扣。
discount 意为“折扣”，指那个减价本身而不是那笔扣款，它历经十六次大减价而在价签上没有标出。
discount 意为“折扣、减价”，指那家店里每一个折扣，每一个角上都挂着同一张做了记号的价签。
discount 意为“折扣”，指留给冬季外套用的那一个，是唯一有人要过两次的。
discount 意为“折扣额、扣款”，指发票上被记入的那笔，会计说这笔扣款就是那张发票的全部。
discount 意为“扣款”，指人人入账却无人解释的那笔而不是那个减价本身，是发票上人人都入账、却无人解释的东西。
discount 意为“折扣”，指通告上写到、被公示的那一个，到 1964 年这个折扣成了通告里的一行。
discount 意为“折扣、打折”，店主十一月写道，整件事的让利是一家店铺和十六次大减价的计算。
discount 意为“折扣”，我记得的是末尾那一个，1979 年给出，至今仍被说成店里最奇的一个。
discount 为抽象总称，助手 1981 年说，一个折扣是唯一会因为被解释清楚而变得更好的东西。
